<!-- Lean towards PR titles that plainly state what was done, rather than trying to convey the spirit of the change. -->

<!-- Keep the whole description short. Rule of thumb: a single sentence per section for a simple change, about 50 words for a mid-difficulty one, more only when needed. Hide extra detail in <details> <summary>...</summary> ... </details>. -->

## Summary

<!-- Explain the why, not what the code does. If non-obvious, give context, rationale and a high-level overview; explain nuance or alternatives. If everything is obvious, write "See title" or a single sentence. As an AI agent, elicit background from a human instead of hypothesizing. -->

## Verification

<!-- Give evidence-based reasoning why the change works. Document what _you_ have done, not a checklist for others. If obviously covered, write "Tests", "Type checker", etc. Changes to agent instructions are tested by the output they produce - point at it. Describe local testing truthfully - never fabricate. Include screenshots/videos for frontend changes and CLI transcripts (command and result, in backticks) for backend ones. Only exceptionally, describe steps that _will_ need to be performed in production once deployed. -->

## Authorship

<!-- Disclose the main author of the PR in only a few words. If the code was AI-generated: the model, harness and level of autonomy (e.g. prescriptive instruction, vague instruction, acting autonomously to solve a goal). If a human wrote it directly, say so. If the description and diff have different authorship, say so. -->
